content.thinking: I should fix the phrasing in CF-4 — "within about a minute" should become something like "almost at once" to avoid implying a precise number, so I'll rewrite it as "The flag went from off to on for every evaluation almost at once."

action_items.item: Require that the service's tests run and pass with a feature flag on before that flag can be switched on in production, covering ordinary account shapes such as a shopper with no purchases this month.
Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after the provider switched it off, and fix how flag changes reach the service.
Alert when the value io-shop evaluates for a flag stays different from the value the provider holds.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.
Roll out flag changes on io-shop in stages: hold at a small share of traffic first, and stop the rollout automatically when the error rate rises.
Make the Mitigation Agent check that a flag revert has reached the service's own evaluations before it judges the candidate refuted.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages failed. The account page error rate, which was typically {Gbac1.6}, reached {Gbac1.5}. The service's share of requests that failed went from {errors_before} before the onset to an average of {errors_while_broken} while it was broken.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors start in the minute of the onset and do not appear in the logs before it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. The production change events read for the day before the onset held only the flag switch, and no deploys came back.
A rollout still in progress. When read at {T10.1}, all replicas ran the same revision.
Shoppers closing their connections. Those ClientDisconnected errors were logged from before the onset, while the account page error rate sat at its usual level, and they stop at the onset.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. In that same minute the service evaluated the flag as on for some of its evaluations, and from the next minute for all of them. Before the switch the service evaluated the flag as off and account pages rendered normally.

With the flag on, the account page divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises at line {F1.1}, the line the incident's log names.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a setting that added a new monthly spending summary to shoppers' account pages, and that summary likely divides by the number of purchases a shopper has made this month, so it breaks for anyone who has not bought anything yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag could be switched on in production, no test was seen that ran the monthly-spend-feature path for a shopper with no purchases this month. Code-Fix's reading says the cases it added would raise against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been caught before the flag reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Switching monthly-spend-feature off at the provider did not reach the service. After Argus switched it off at {P2.1}, the service still logged every evaluation of the flag as on.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The revert would have taken the failing path out of use at the service and shortened the incident, instead of being judged not to help and put back.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was linked to no on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been on the incident while it ran and could have seen that the service still evaluated the flag as on after the revert.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for every evaluation almost at once, and no staged rollout was seen that would stop it if errors rose.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failure before the rollout stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well: The Investigator Agent formed a candidate naming the monthly-spend-feature switch {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent reverted the flag {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service itself rather than assuming the revert had worked, and put the flag back when the service stayed at the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request with a proposed fix and tests {T36.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The revert was judged refuted even though the logs showed the service still evaluating the flag as on after it was switched off. The revert never reached the service, so the verdict did not test the candidate.

In the second investigation the candidate itself noted that the flag still showed as on, yet it was marked refuted as tested for the first candidate. Argus then moved to FIXING saying no explanation was left to try, rather than following up on why the revert had not reached the service.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page works out a shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing this month's spend by the number of purchases made this month, and nothing guards against that number being zero. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature back on and the division still in the code, account pages could keep failing, likely for shoppers with no purchases this month, and switching the flag off at the provider was not seen to stop the service evaluating it as on.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again in a way that reaches io-shop. Then confirm at the service that its logs show the flag evaluated as off, that the ZeroDivisionError lines from src/io_shop/spend_summary.py stop, and that the error rate falls back to near {errors_before}.
